intro: Cairo grew its modern quarters in the 1860s under Khedive Ismail, who laid out boulevards and gardens on European lines and, by one account, brought banyan trees from India to plant in them. On Zamalek, the island in the Nile, one of those banyans still stands beside the street to the Cairo Tower, dropping its aerial roots into new trunks. A reader sent us its photograph.

trees.name: The Zamalek Banyan

location.address: Al Borg street, near the Cairo Tower, Zamalek (Gezira), Cairo

trees.story:
"Every Egyptian knows this tree," wrote the reader who sent us this photograph from Zamalek, the island in the Nile at the heart of Cairo. "It's very loved and celebrated here."

It is an Indian banyan, and its history runs back to Khedive Ismail, the ruler who rebuilt Cairo on European lines in the 1860s. Egyptian Streets, which wrote about the tree in 2022, says he imported banyans from India in 1868 and planted them in Garden City, Azbakeya and Zamalek; it puts this one at about 150 years old, on Al Borg street, the road people take to the Cairo Tower. The reader gives the same story and wonders whether it is the only one left. Another old banyan grows in the gardens of the Manial Palace on Roda island.

The photograph is taken from below, looking up into the crown. Grey limbs reach out in every direction, and from them hang curtains of aerial roots, some still thin as rope, others grown into pillars as thick as trunks, the way a banyan walks outward over the years. A low wall and an iron railing stand in front of it.

Walk along the railing and look for where the hanging roots have reached the ground.
